issues.evidence: R4 value is '?' in schematic and PCB. R4 is the only connection from VCC to U1 (ADM2486) pin 7 PV. Net-(U1-PV) has just R4.2 and U1.7.
issues.why_it_matters: On the ADM2486, PV (power valid) is an input that has to be driven high for the part to work. If R4 is unpopulated, or the assembler cannot pick a part for '?', PV floats and RS-485 may never work. The part needs a real value (for example 10k or 0R).

issues.evidence: R27 (VBUS to A, failsafe pull-up), R28 (A to B, termination) and R29 (B to GND1, failsafe pull-down) all have value '?' and no DNP flag.
issues.why_it_matters: The RS-485 bias and termination resistors probably depend on where the board sits on the bus. Even so, the BOM cannot be ordered or assembled without values or DNP marking. Fitting a 120R terminator on every node would load the bus.

issues.evidence: PS1 has schematic value 'B1209', MP field 'RO-0505S' (RECOM, 5V in / 5V out), symbol and footprint 'RO-0505S', and PCB value 'B1212S'. The input comes from J1 pin 1, which also feeds U7 (L78L05). That supply must therefore be at least 7V, nominally 12V.
issues.why_it_matters: The 12V bus supply would destroy an RO-0505S (5V input) ordered from the MP field. Three different part names for one isolated converter is a likely ordering mistake.

issues.evidence: J1 is a field-wired screw terminal (V+, A, B, GND). Pin 1 V+ goes straight to U7 VI and PS1 +VIN with only 100n caps (C1, C6). There is no series diode or fuse, and no TVS on the supply. A and B have only the 50mA polyfuses F9 and F10, with no TVS.
issues.why_it_matters: A swapped V+/GND on a bus cable reverse-biases the 78L05 and the isolated DC-DC and can kill both. Long RS-485/power cables also pick up surges.

issues.evidence: R1 is 4k7 in a 1206 footprint. R2 and R7 are 4k7 in 0805 (all other resistors are 0805). There is no electrical reason for a 1206 I2C pull-up.
issues.why_it_matters: One extra BOM line or reel for the same value.

issues.evidence: Values in the PCB differ from the schematic: PS1 B1212S vs B1209, R5 and R6 '?' vs '10', C7 '?' vs '100n'.
issues.why_it_matters: A BOM or position file generated from the PCB would carry stale or missing values. The copper is not affected.

acceptable_designs.reason: The FM24C64B F-RAM has internal pull-downs on A0-A2 and WP. Leaving them open gives address 0x50 with writes enabled, and 0x50 does not clash with the INA228 at 0x40.
ADM2486 pin 10 DE is a driver-enable status output, not an input, so leaving it open is fine. Pins 11 and 14 are NC.
Both sides of the isolator are bypassed: VDD1 by C10 (about 2.8mm away) and VDD2 by C9 and C2 (about 2.6 and 3.6mm). Every other IC also has its own 100n within 5mm (U2-C4, U3-C5, U4-C3/C16).
GND (meter/shunt side) and GND1 (RS-485 bus side) are deliberately separate. The only links are the ADM2486 isolation barrier and the isolated DC-DC PS1, with separate copper zones.
Both J2 terminals are on the same net on purpose: it is a sense or loop-through terminal routed to the JP5 voltage-sense selector.
INA228 VBUS is chosen by solder-jumper options JP3/JP5 (shunt high side or external J2) to suit how the meter is installed. It is open only before configuration.
D2 is driven low-side by PA7 with R56 (220R) on the anode side, so current limiting is present.
4k7 pull-ups to VCC are present (R1, R2), and /ALERT has R7.

notes: Pinouts checked against my datasheet knowledge: ATtiny1624 SOIC-14 (TWI on PB0/PB1, USART1 on PA1/PA2 for RS-485, USART0 TX on PB2 for debug), INA228 VSSOP-10, ADM2486 SOIC-16W, L78L05 TO-92 (1=OUT, 2=GND, 3=IN), RECOM/Mornsun SIP4 converter (1=-Vin, 2=+Vin, 3=-Vout, 4=+Vout). All match. RE and RTS tied together to PA4 is normal half-duplex. In the PCB, the zones are not filled in the file. Isolation spacing between bus-side and meter-side copper is at least ~2.4mm, limited by the converter's own SIP pin pitch, which is fine for functional isolation. I did not check creepage against any safety standard. I did not open the ADM2486 datasheet online; PV/DE pin semantics are from memory.
